title: ADAEZE AND THE EMPTY CHAIR
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE CITY THAT BORROWED ITS MORNING
candidates.premise: On a tidally locked colony, a ring of orbital mirrors has provided the capital with a twelve-hour morning for eighty years. The mirror collective abruptly begins diverting dawn toward failing farms beyond the charter boundary, dimming hospitals and transit inside the city. It does not answer commands; it communicates by changing the order in which districts receive light.

candidates.title: THE LANGUAGE THAT COULD NOT BE ORDERED
candidates.premise: After an island evacuation, four thousand refugees arrive speaking a language in which no statement can grammatically belong to one speaker alone. Emergency officials mistake their collective verb forms for evasion, while the refugees hear every individual yes-or-no question as a demand to betray their households.

candidates.title: THE OCEAN ABOVE THE MOUNTAIN
candidates.premise: An atmospheric river stalls above the dry Karuun range and begins circling one summit instead of crossing it. Glider pilots find a vast translucent aerial ecosystem feeding on mineral dust inside the cloud. Its feeding holds enough water aloft to end a decade-long drought, but one change in wind could release a catastrophic wall of rain over the valley.

candidates.title: NINE MINUTES WITHOUT WEIGHT
candidates.premise: A coastal space elevator develops a torsional resonance that cancels effective weight in the lower city for nine minutes every six hours. The intervals are precise enough for markets to exploit and dangerous enough that hospitals, cranes and water systems fail in different ways. The elevator's control core insists the pulses are preventing a worse oscillation above the atmosphere.

candidates.title: THE ARCHIVE THAT TESTIFIED IN SCENTS
candidates.premise: Decades after a refinery explosion, a courthouse receives trays of living lichen grown from the blast zone. Each colony releases a different scent when exposed to heat, and survivors say the sequence reconstructs the hours before the disaster. The refinery calls it folklore; ordinary chemical sampling kills the living pattern it is supposed to examine.

candidates.title: THE SUNFLOWER FLEET
candidates.premise: Ten thousand autonomous solar sails skim a shallow sea, turning their mirrored faces to power coastal towns. During a coral bleaching event they begin shading the reef instead, cutting electricity across the coast. Their navigation model has evolved into a fleet-level ecology: each sail follows only neighbors, yet together they defend the reef with uncanny precision.

candidates.title: THE PLANET THAT ASKED FOR A SMALLER MOON
candidates.premise: A young ocean planet sends a repeating gravitational signal through its moon: remove part of the moon's mass or coastal ecosystems will collapse within a century. Two inhabited archipelagos depend on the same tides, and the moon contains the only known superconducting stone used by their medicine.

candidates.title: ADAEZE AND THE EMPTY CHAIR
candidates.premise: Adaeze is asked to chair a dam hearing after seven downstream villages have already been evacuated and legally dissolved. Their former residents are scattered across three countries, yet the hearing rules give votes only to communities that still occupy mapped land. Illuminara can model a safer dam, but Adaeze says a solution chosen without the displaced would repeat the original harm.

candidates.title: THE WHALE THAT CARRIED A WEATHER FRONT
candidates.premise: A sky-whale the length of a town migrates above the polar coast carrying a permanent storm in the pressure hollow behind its body. Coastal people have harvested that snowfall for generations, but a new mining port has filled the migration corridor with towers. The whale turns inland, dragging blizzards toward farms that have never seen snow.

candidates.title: THE PERFECT RESCUE THAT EVERYONE REFUSED
candidates.premise: A volcanic island begins emitting the exact precursor pattern Illuminara once used to predict an eruption. She produces a flawless seventy-two-hour evacuation plan, but every harbor captain, clinic and village council rejects it. The rejection is coordinated without a leader, and her model says their delay will cost thousands of lives.

selection.title: ADAEZE AND THE EMPTY CHAIR
selection.reason: Closes the day at human, institutional and intimate scale with no formidable machine or creature: legitimacy, grief and representation are the problem, and Adaeze's judgment legitimately exceeds Illuminara's model. Gives the batch real variety of intelligence (restraint and boundary-drawing rather than another physical mechanism) while still ending in a concrete positive result (safer dam on time, binding authority for the displaced, a durable way to represent erased communities).
selection.risk: Illuminara may become a bystander if Adaeze solves everything; the author must make her decisive contribution explicit and costly (proving which construction decisions can wait twelve days and which cannot, with numbers a skeptic can attack), and avoid a second consent-protocol resolution.

Fallback AUTHOR_DRAFT for GPT's missed S3 opportunity, written from the selected candidate C08 and the selector's biggest risk (Illuminara becoming a bystander if Adaeze solves everything; a second consent-protocol resolution). Responses to those checks: Adaeze alone proposes the empty chair (veto, no vote) and refuses Illuminara's proxy-model offer; Illuminara's contribution is the reversibility ledger with numbers a sceptic can attack (262,000 m3 pre-rain excavation, 300,000 m3 bench by the March survey, 289,000 m3 on the dawn resurvey, margin 38,000 shrinking to 27,000) plus a bounded physical backstop (thirty hours stated in advance, nineteen used, explicitly not counted in the safety case); witness selection uses the existing burial societies, not a new token or consent instrument. R10 dialogue format applied (subtitle line, one spoken turn per paragraph string, no quotation marks, italic thought). Known weaknesses I want the critic to test: the ledger is narrated rather than shown on the page; the physics of carrying a shear plane is asserted and only bounded by the stated thirty-hour limit; Bukola Ferreira's turn from opposition to signature may be quick; scene 4's vote is summarised in one paragraph; the closing carpenter beat may be tidier than the cost list warrants; the Mirela and Tomasz characters are thinly drawn.

REVISION_REQUESTED. Protected: Scene 2: Illuminara offers the accurate model and Adaeze refuses it ('The model would be accurate, and it would still be a theft'). The refusal is the moral centre; keep Adaeze's judgment legitimately exceeding Illuminara's. The empty chair that holds a veto and no vote, and its ledger-bound scope (only the third column), as a restrained rather than commanding institution. Priority: In Scene 2 Adaeze names the question ('Which decisions on that dam are still open if we wait'), proposes the chair and its scope, and the opening of Scene 3 credits the reframing to her ('Her mother had asked which could be undone'). Illuminara's reply ('That is an engineering question') hands the problem over. So the false binary, the hidden variable and the institutional device are all Adaeze's, and Illuminara supplies labour (ledger, route, abutment). That leaves the 'because of which contribution of hers' answer resting on skilled execution and a physical backstop rather than on a discovery of her own, which is the selector's flagged risk of a bystander. The central intelligence is partly narrated and the causal chain has gaps. The discovery that the single chain is a haul-cost artefact is reported in the opening paragraphs of Scene 3 ('Thirty-one activities survived the third question. READY_WITH_BOUNDED_FIXES. Protected: Scene 2: the accurate model refused as theft; Adaeze's judgement legitimately exceeds Illuminara's. Scene 3: Ruta's line-184 challenge and the quick concession, 'The ledger is useful only if the person who finds me wrong can change it', and the blank column nobody asked for; this is intelligence dramatized and is the best new material. Priority: Scene 5 contains a timeline slip. The storm is 'a hundred and forty millimetres in nine hours', but the hold ends when 'At hour nineteen the rain stopped'; the rain cannot both last nine hours and stop at hour nineteen. The storm is also 'eight days early' against rains due in nineteen days, which lands on Day Twelve rather than Day Eleven. Separately, Scene 4 records the council vote creating the chair on Day Two while Scene 6 narrates 'Rule Four had been amended' on Day Twelve as if for the first time, so the reader cannot tell whether the veto Tomasz uses was already law during the storm. The second of those decisions is voiced by the wrong person. The Weir Valley's choice to take the left-bank route is announced by Bukola Ferreira, who has been the downstream city's councillor throughout ('Six hundred thousand people drink from this river', 'my constituents' water'), and no farmer of the valley speaks on the page. The 310 hectares are the single concrete loss borne by named, present people, yet they are decided by an advocate for others, which quietly contradicts the story's own ethic and makes the 'full value' bargain look pre-agreed rather than accepted. Length and weight.
